outcome: Mode of birth (vaginal birth vs. cesarean section)
cohort: Nulliparous women, women with previous vaginal birth, and women with previous LSCS
finding: While ultrasound-measured LUS distensibility was a significant predictor of vaginal birth in nulliparous women and those with previous vaginal births, it did not predict successful VBAC.
mod_finding: Although trends towards lesser distensibility were observed in the VBAC group who delivered vaginally, these did not reach statistical significance, indicating that ultrasound-measured LUS distensibility was not a reliable predictor of successful VBAC.
